No. Cold welding also requires a vacuum, which would not be present on the surface of Earth. Earth has basically always had some type of atmosphere, even before oxygen.

It also requires a significant amount of pressure (in the thousands of psi) to be applied to a joint.

Edit: The high pressures are to get a stable joint as strong as the source materials, minimal pressures are required to get materials to just "stick" together.

Let’s break this bullshit down before it even gets flight. Many people are saying in this thread about not dusting and laziness but this is not related in the slightest. This study follows the classic science news loop: http://www.phdcomics.com/comics.php?n=1174

The researchers have been examining molecules that are semi-volatile compounds (SVOCs).

Here is a list of some organic ones:

http://www.epa.gov/reg3hwmd/bf-lr/regional/analytical/semi-volatile.htm

They found that dust did contain these compounds as many of these SVOCs are in household items. They did an gene assay of 30 different SVOCs. This is adding the chemical to see if it binds with the a specific receptor: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma 1.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peroxisome_proliferator-activated_receptor
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peroxisome_proliferator-activated_receptor_gamma

These chemicals did bind to the receptor somewhat (called an agonist). This receptor is related to storing fat and sugar metabolism, There are drugs like Rosiglitazone, the control drug they used in the study, which is a drug for diabetes – it lowers blood sugar. The news presentation is much different from the truth. Dust causes obesity is a nice clickbait title, but the truth is (and I quote the fucking authors), these chemicals “are possible PPARγ1 agonists” and “can activate human PPARγ1 in a transfected cell culture system”. Transfection is the process of forcing DNA into a cell.

This entire paper is: Some of these molecules can sometimes bind to a receptor that is used in the process of metabolism. Can it cause obesity? Well that is a huge fucking leap from a lab experiment.

Is it possible it can increase the rate of obesity? Yes. It is also possible it decreases obesity as it binds to the same receptors as diabetic medication, cause a chemical cascade or have the body reach a homeostasis around the SVOCs. We don’t know. Interesting research, but to quote the paper “further research is needed to identify the primary chemical(s) driving this activity”. The authors know that it a strong leap to make, but they will push the idea for more funding :D.
